content.text:
The final pass is done. I found and fixed three requirement gaps plus some polish, and everything passes. The physics results are unchanged: same settings give the bit-identical outcome in Node and Chrome, at every screen size. `index.html` is again the only file in the folder.

**Requirement gaps fixed:**
- **Simulation stopped too early.** Once the verdict fired (after 1.5 s of near-stillness or a 40 s cap), physics stopped and any bricks still creeping froze in place. It now keeps stepping until every body is asleep (hard cap 120 s after impact) and refreshes the result card at the end. The time label reads "debris settling" then "all at rest".
- **Active parameters disappeared at 1180 px wide or less.** A compact line (car speed and mass, wall size, brick mass, pending changes) now sits in the telemetry panel on those screens. On short screens the momentum/energy row gives way so the panel doesn't cover the car.
- **80 px/m was only nominal.** The view always zoomed to fit (about 0.5–0.65× on laptops). A new Fit / 1:1 toggle (button bottom-right, or Z) renders at a true 80 px/m and follows the car. The scale bar labels which mode you're in.

**Performance:**
- **Heavy walls are now smooth.** The per-frame physics budget stops before a step would overrun the frame. The 1,960-brick wall now runs at 60 fps in slow motion (about 0.46× real time) instead of stuttering near 30 fps. The on-screen rate readout shows the slowdown.
- **Two small engine speedups.** All bodies share one object shape, and contact manifolds are iterated as an array instead of a `Map`. Both are bit-identical, but only worth a few percent; this machine was too loaded (load average 17) to measure better. Bigger gains would mean fewer solver iterations or a different broadphase, which would change the physics, so I didn't do that in a final pass.

**Polish:**
- Car momentum no longer shows "-0.0" when the car stops.
- The Displaced stat also shows how many bricks have fallen.
- The pending note now says settings apply on Test or Reset (Reset already applied them).
- The keyboard shortcuts (Space, R, S, Z) are listed in the settings panel.
- In low-gravity, low-friction runs where debris slides past the 40 s verdict cap, "settled in" now reports the real rest time instead of 40 s.

**Checks run:**
- **Default run:** impact at 22.0 m/s, 14.1 g peak, 12 cm crush, all 200 bricks down, all at rest at 7.8 s.
- **Sweep:** 11 configurations covering every slider extreme, with no NaNs, no bricks below ground, and everything asleep at the end.
- **Mass and speed change the outcome:**
  - At 6 m/s into 12 kg bricks the wall is shoved but stays standing (2 fallen).
  - A 500 kg car at 30 m/s into an 11.5 t wall barely moves it.
  - A 4,000 kg car at 45 m/s takes all 400 bricks down.
- **Browser:** tested at 360, 1000, 1280 and 1440 px wide, with the console clean every time. Idle edits, clamping, Restore defaults, Space, edits during a run, R, S and Z all work.That notification is the settings sweep I already covered in my last summary. All 11 configurations came out stable, with no NaNs, no bricks below ground, and every body at rest at the end. The one issue it turned up, "settled in" showing 40 s when debris kept sliding past the verdict cap, is already fixed. Nothing else to do.
